description: The MEDIA of an app: photos, textures, sounds, videos and 3D models (glb), many, apart from the app's files (neblla_upload_file is for code, 300 files for a free account's apps together, each counted once per app whether in pre, pro or both, with versions and neblla_promote). Media have no versions and no deploy: a change is live at once, in pre and pro, and the app reads them with neblla.media (it sees the change on its next read, without touching its code). They are in COLLECTIONS (made when first named), in an order, each item with a card: title, text, alt and your own fields. An image gets WebP variants (320, 640, 1280, 2048 wide, never wider than the original) and keeps its original as it came. The space is a bag of the ACCOUNT: 100 MB shared by the apps of its free projects, originals and variants (a Pro project has its own 2 GB for its apps). One file up to 25 MB. Actions: "collections" → { collections: [{ collection, key, count, bytes }], usage: { scope, used, limit, free } }; "list" { collection, offset?, limit? } → the items in order, each { id, position, title, text, alt, fields, note?, width, height, url, srcset, variants, original, bytes }; "get" { id }; NOTE FOR YOU: an item may carry "note", written for the developer's AI and never shown to users. Neblla Creator leaves one on what it exports to the collection "creator" (what the file is and how to use it in client.js: e.g. a sprite atlas, sprites.png and sprites.json, Aseprite format, animations walk and jump): read it before using the file. A JSON file (an atlas's map, a level) is kind "data". "upload" { collection, items: [{ contentUrl | content, title?, text?, alt?, fields? }] (up to 50), position?: "end" | "start", resize? } → { uploaded, skipped?, failed?, oversized?, usage }: each item on its own (a failed one says why, the same bytes already in the app are skipped with the id that has them); TOO BIG FOR A SCREEN: the original is kept as it came. An image over 2560 px on its long side carries "oversized" (and the upload a summary "oversized"): what it takes, what it would take reduced, what that saves and how many more would fit in the bag, with a message. Tell the developer those numbers and ASK whether to reduce: never decide it yourself, a texture, a map or an original to print may need every pixel. "resize": true (to the screen size) or a long side in px reduces at upload, when the developer already said so. "shrink" { ids | collection, maxSide?, dryRun? } reduces later the images over maxSide (default 2560), up to 50 per call ("remaining" says how many are left): the item keeps its id, card and place, its original is replaced and its variants made again, so THE BIG ORIGINAL IS LOST (say so, and confirm first). dryRun: true says what it would save without changing anything. "update" { id, title?, text?, alt?, note?, fields? (merged; null removes a field), replaceFields? }; "move" { ids, collection, position? } moves them to that collection, in that order (e.g. "these 40 go to Bodas"); "reorder" { collection, ids } puts those first, in that order, the rest after as they were (e.g. "the lighthouse one first": ids [its id]); "delete" { ids } (confirm first: it cannot be undone); "create_collection" { collection }; "rename_collection" { collection, newName }; "delete_collection" { collection, withItems? } (refused with collection_not_empty unless withItems: true). PRIVATE ORIGINALS, files to sell (C230): a photo in high resolution, a score in PDF, an ebook (pdf, epub), a pack of textures (zip), a song in wav or flac. "private" { ids | collection, private: true | false, publicWidth? } keeps the original in a bucket that is never public: the public read gives only the variants up to publicWidth px wide (default 1280; none wider is made) and never the original, and says private: true with unlockedBy. On a collection it stays so for its new uploads (up to 50 per call, "remaining" says how many are left). Upload private from the start with "upload" { private: true, publicWidth? }: a file that was public may stay in the caches of whoever had it. "link" { productId, ids | collection } makes a product unlock those files or the whole collection; "unlink" undoes it. A one_time product: the buyer keeps them for good; a subscription: while it is alive (e.g. an academy's library of scores). To sell ONE file per credit from a collection ("a pack of 5 downloads to choose from Agua"): a credit kind with unlocks: ["agua"] in neblla_update_app business.credits, and a product that gives those credits. The user downloads with neblla.media.download(id) in the app: Neblla checks their session and right and gives a link straight from the bucket for a few minutes (a new one each click; one passed on stops working). "holders" { id } → who has the right to a file (buyers, live subscribers, who used a credit); "download_link" { id } → a link for you, the developer. Errors: media_storage_off, media_private_storage_off (Neblla has no private bucket yet), invalid_public_width, private_required, product_not_found, product_cannot_unlock (only one_time and subscription), not_private, invalid_resize, ids_or_collection_required, media_quota_exceeded (scope, used, limit, needs), media_too_large, media_type_not_supported, media_fetch_failed (reason), collection_not_found, collection_exists, collection_full, media_not_found, invalid_fields.

collection.description: The collection, by its name ("Bodas") or key ("bodas")

dryRun.description: For shrink: say what it would save, change nothing

fields.description: For update: merged into the card; null removes a field

id.description: For get, update, holders and download_link

ids.description: For move, reorder, delete, shrink, private, link and unlink

alt.description: What the image shows, for screen readers and search engines

content.description: The file as base64 (or a data: URI), when there is no URL. The whole call is limited to ~8 MB, so a URL for anything big

contentUrl.description: Public URL of the file: Neblla downloads it (preferred: e.g. the original of a photo on the old site)

fields.description: The developer's own fields: { year: 2023, size: "70 x 45 cm", price: 520, available: true }

name.description: The original file name, kept for reference

note.description: A note for the developer's AI, never shown to users: what the file is and how client.js uses it

text.description: A longer text: a caption, a description

maxSide.description: For shrink: the long side to reduce to, in px (default 2560)

note.description: For update: the note for the developer's AI (null removes it)

position.description: For upload and move: at the end (default) or the start of the collection

private.description: For private (required) and upload: the original is private, unlocked by a purchase

productId.description: For link and unlink: a one_time product or a subscription of the app

publicWidth.description: For private and upload: the widest variant the public sees of a private image, in px (default 1280)

replaceFields.description: For update: the fields given replace all of them

resize.description: For upload: true reduces the images bigger than a screen needs, a number to that long side in px; only when the developer asked

withItems.description: For delete_collection: delete its items too

name: neblla_media
